<!-- Generated by esquadro docs from the blueprint's manifest: do not edit. -->

The project's environments (development, staging and production) and its environment variables, all declared in the model: by the blueprints that read them and in app.esq's env blocks. It writes .env.example, with every variable documented, and keeps a .env.&lt;environment> file per environment (yours, out of git): new variables are added, commented, and your values never change. The app reads its environment's file, picked by APP_ENV, and the env command shows where each value comes from, secrets hidden. In development everything has a value, so the project runs as it is.

```esquadro
blueprint env
```

## Works with

- **Requires** [app](../app/): the app must use them too.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environments` | list | `["development", "staging", "production"]` | The environments, in order; the first is where development happens, the one APP_ENV defaults to. |

```esquadro
blueprint env {
  environments ["development", "staging", "production"]
}
```

## Hooks

- `post-gen` files, edits `.env.development`, `.env.staging`, `.env.production`, `.gitignore`
